title: Script Sensitivity: Benchmarking Language Models on Unicode, Romanized and Mixed-Script Sinhala
what_it_does: Benchmarks 24 open LMs on native Unicode vs romanized vs mixed-script Sinhala with language fixed.
key_results: Over 300x median perplexity degradation from native Unicode to romanized Sinhala; single-script evaluation underestimates deployment risk.
gap_vs_ours: Script duality with language fixed, but no LLM-as-judge and no content-quality scoring; supports the mechanism behind our hypothesis.

title: Indi-RomCoM: Code-Mixed Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Romanized Indic-English Instructions
what_it_does: Benchmarks LLMs on romanized code-mixed Indic-English instructions across 7 tasks and 4 Indic languages with controlled code-mixing density.
key_results: LLMs consistently underperform on romanized code-mixed instructions, degrading with code-mixing density.
drawbacks: Task-performance benchmark; instructions vary rather than holding content fixed.
gap_vs_ours: No judge-scoring bias; no native-script twin condition for a judge to score.

title: BabelJudge: Measuring LLM-as-a-Judge Reliability Across Languages and Agent Trajectories
what_it_does: Framework measuring judge position bias, verbosity bias, order inconsistency, and cross-lingual degradation across English, Hindi, Arabic, Swahili via controlled perturbations.
key_results: Documents judge reliability degradation across languages including Hindi.
drawbacks: Hindi appears in native Devanagari only.
gap_vs_ours: No script/transliteration condition at all; language, not script, is the variable.

title: Towards Reliable Multilingual LLMs-as-a-Judge: An Empirical Study
what_it_does: Empirical study of building multilingual LLM judges (English/Spanish/Basque): instruction translation, mono vs multilingual supervision, model size.
key_results: Characterizes low-resource judge weaknesses and supervision strategies.
drawbacks: All three languages are Latin-script; no Indic languages.
gap_vs_ours: No script, transliteration, or romanization dimension.

title: One Language, Two Scripts: Probing Script-Invariance in LLM Concept Representations
what_it_does: Uses Serbian Cyrillic/Latin digraphia to probe whether LLM internal concept representations are script-invariant.
key_results: Finds imperfect cross-script transfer: script non-invariance exists inside models.
drawbacks: Interpretability probing only; Serbian, not Devanagari/romanized Indic.
gap_vs_ours: The exact same-language-two-scripts control paradigm, but at representation level with no judge-scoring outcome.

title: Toward Robust LLM-Based Judges: Taxonomic Bias Evaluation and Debiasing Optimization (JudgeBiasBench)
what_it_does: Taxonomy of 12 LLM-judge bias types across 4 dimensions with bias-augmented instances and RL/contrastive debiasing.
drawbacks: Script/orthography/romanization is not among the taxonomized bias types.
gap_vs_ours: Direct evidence the community has not yet named script bias in judges; our paper fills the missing taxonomy slot.
